Get started with tflspec

Source: vignettes/articles/tflspec.Rmd
tflspec.Rmd

tflspec reads the specifications of a study’s tables, listings and figures (Excel workbooks, YAML for figures) and writes the R program each one stands for. The program is the deliverable: short, readable, written the way a person would write it, and needing only cards / cardx and rtfreporter to run – not tflspec. People copy it into the study, read it, and finish it.

ADaM ──(ARD spec)──> ARD ──(table spec)──> plan ──(report spec)──> RTF
          tfl_ard_code()      tfl_table_code()       tfl_report_code()
          tfl_build_ard()     tfl_table_plan()       tfl_report()

Each spec can be written out as code (the *_code() functions) or run (tfl_build_ard(), tfl_table_plan(), tfl_report()). Both come from the same list of steps, so the object and the program cannot disagree.

This article walks the whole flow for one table, a demographics table (DM), using the workbooks that come with the package and its oncology sample study’s ADaM data (adsl, adae …; see ?adsl).

library(tflspec)
library(rtfreporter)

A study folder

Every path in a spec is relative to the study folder, and the generated programs run from it. Ours holds two ADaM datasets:

study <- file.path(tempdir(), "study")
dir.create(file.path(study, "data"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(adsl, file.path(study, "data", "adsl.rds"))
saveRDS(adae, file.path(study, "data", "adae.rds"))

1. The ARD spec: what is analysed

The ARD spec is a workbook of a few sheets: study (keys such as the subject key), datasets (what is read, and columns derived on reading), populations (the analysis sets), analysis_data (named data the analyses read, each a report’s own; optional) and analyses, one cards / cardx call per row. A study normally keeps it as an .xlsx; here it is written from R so the whole article runs on its own.

df <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ard_spec <- tfl_ard_spec(list(
  study = df(key = c("id", "output"),
             value = c("USUBJID", "output/ard/ard.rds")),
  datasets = df(dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),
                path = c("data/adsl.rds", "data/adae.rds"),
                derive = c('BSLDGR1 = ifelse(BSLD < 60, "<60 mm", ">=60 mm")', NA)),
  populations = df(population_id = "SAF", dataset = "ADSL",
                   where = 'SAFFL == "Y"'),
  analyses = df(output_id = "DM",
                analysis_id = c("BIGN", "ARMN", "CONT", "CAT"),
                method = c("total_n", "categorical", "continuous",
                           "categorical"),
                population_id = "SAF",
                by = c(NA, NA, "TRT01A", "TRT01A"),
                variables = c(NA, "TRT01A", "AGE | BSLD",
                              "AGEGR1 | SEX | RACE | ECOGBL"))))

path <- tfl_write_ard_spec(ard_spec, file.path(study, "ard_spec.xlsx"))
ard_spec <- tfl_read_ard_spec(path)
ard_spec$analyses[, c("output_id", "analysis_id", "method", "by", "variables")]
#>   output_id analysis_id      method     by                    variables
#> 1        DM        BIGN     total_n   <NA>                         <NA>
#> 2        DM        ARMN categorical   <NA>                       TRT01A
#> 3        DM        CONT  continuous TRT01A                   AGE | BSLD
#> 4        DM         CAT categorical TRT01A AGEGR1 | SEX | RACE | ECOGBL

ARMN counts the subjects of each arm: the column header’s (N=xx) is read from it. method is a keyword (tfl_ard_methods()), any pkg::function of cards or cardx, or a function of the study’s own. The article The ARD spec goes through every sheet.

The ARD program

tfl_ard_code() writes the program. It reads the data, makes the analysis set, and calls cards once per analysis:

cat(tfl_ard_code(ard_spec, part = "body"), sep = "\n")
report_id <- "DM"

# ---- data ----
adsl <- readRDS("data/adsl.rds") |> mutate(BSLDGR1 = ifelse(BSLD < 60, "<60 mm", ">=60 mm"))

# ---- populations ----
# adsl_sub: SAF (SAFFL == "Y")
adsl_sub <- filter(adsl, SAFFL == "Y")

# ---- analyses ----
# BIGN
ard_bign <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_total_n() |>
  fmt_ard(fmt_default) |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "BIGN", population = "SAF")

# ARMN
ard_armn <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_tabulate(variables = TRT01A, fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "ARMN", population = "SAF")

# CONT
ard_cont <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_summary(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = c(AGE, BSLD),
    fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default
  ) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "CONT", population = "SAF")

# CAT
ard_cat <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_tabulate(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = c(AGEGR1, SEX, RACE, ECOGBL),
    fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default
  ) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "CAT", population = "SAF")

# the report's rows of the study ARD, with the fingerprint of its
# definition (tfl_ard_spec_hash())
bind_rows(ard_bign, ard_armn, ard_cont, ard_cat) |>
  save_ard(report_id, definition = "8e9ceecd4874efbfa7321bfdc46e2809")

part = "body" leaves out the setup every program starts with (the packages, the helpers that tag each result with its output_id / analysis_id); tfl_ard_code(ard_spec) writes the whole file, ready to save as programs/ard.R.

The ARD

tfl_build_ard() runs that same program from the study folder and saves the study ARD where the study key output says:

ard <- tfl_build_ard(ard_spec, dir = study)
ard[1:6, c("output_id", "analysis_id", "variable", "stat_name", "stat")]
#> # An ARD data frame: 6 × 5
#>   output_id analysis_id variable        stat_name    stat
#>   <chr>     <chr>       <chr>           <chr>      <list>
#> 1 DM        BIGN        ..ard_total_n.. N         158    
#> 2 DM        ARMN        TRT01A          n          80    
#> 3 DM        ARMN        TRT01A          N         158    
#> 4 DM        ARMN        TRT01A          p           0.506
#> 5 DM        ARMN        TRT01A          n          78    
#> 6 DM        ARMN        TRT01A          N         158

2. The table spec: how the ARD becomes a table

The table spec says which keys go across (cols) and down (rows), the labels and order of each variable, the cell templates and digits, the pages, the column header. The package’s example DM.xlsx defines this table:

ex <- system.file("extdata", "ard-spec", package = "tflspec")
spec <- tfl_read_report_spec(file.path(ex, c("report.xlsx", "DM.xlsx")),
                             output_id = "DM")
spec$cells[, c("variable", "row", "template", "digits")]
#>      variable       row           template digits
#> 1  continuous         n                {N}      0
#> 2  continuous Mean (SD)      {mean} ({sd})    1,2
#> 3  continuous    Median           {median}      1
#> 4  continuous  Min, Max       {min}, {max}      0
#> 5 categorical      <NA> {n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})   <NA>

tfl_read_report_spec() reads the table sheets and the report sheets together (one object serves both); tfl_read_table_spec() reads the table sheets alone.

The table program

tfl_table_code() writes the rtfreporter plan: the roles in table_plan(), then one plan_*() verb for each thing the sheets say.

cat(tfl_table_code(spec, pipe = "|>"), sep = "\n")
# the code lists: each value in its order, as the table shows it
cl_agegr1 <- c("<65", ">=65")
cl_sex <- c("F", "M")
cl_ecogbl <- c("0", "1")

plan <- ard |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "TRT01A", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(
    continuous = list(
      n = "{N:.0f}",
      "Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
      Median = "{median:.1f}",
      "Min, Max" = "{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"
    ),
    categorical = "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})"
  ) |>
  plan_levels(
    variable = c("AGE", "AGEGR1", "SEX", "RACE", "ECOGBL", "BSLD"),
    AGEGR1 = cl_agegr1,
    SEX = cl_sex,
    ECOGBL = cl_ecogbl
  ) |>
  plan_labels(
    variable = c(
      AGE = "Age (years)",
      AGEGR1 = "Age group, n (%)",
      SEX = "Sex, n (%)",
      RACE = "Race, n (%)",
      ECOGBL = "Baseline ECOG performance status, n (%)",
      BSLD = "Baseline sum of diameters (mm)"
    )
  ) |>
  plan_digits(rounding = "sas") |>
  plan_col_header(
    data.frame(
      line = c("1", "1", "2", "2"),
      cols = c("row_label", ".values", "row_label", ".values"),
      span = c(NA, "each", NA, "each"),
      text = c(NA, "{col}", "Parameter", "(N={n})")
    )
  ) |>
  plan_stub(name = "row_label", before = TRUE) |>
  plan_blanks(where = "between_groups", first = TRUE, last = FALSE) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 30, split = "group_safe") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(row_label = 4, .values = 2)) |>
  plan_style(align_count_pct = TRUE)

The table

tfl_table_plan() builds that same plan from an ARD. Being a plan, a verb piped after it still wins – one report’s own change, in one line, without touching the workbook:

data <- normalize_ard(tfl_ard_for(ard, "DM"))
plan <- tfl_table_plan(data, spec) |>
  plan_cells(notes = FALSE)

The table it makes (plan_apply(stage = "table") stops before the pages):

knitr::kable(plan_apply(plan, stage = "table"))

3. The report spec: the document around the table

The report spec dresses the page: paper and margins, the running header and footer, titles and footnotes, tokens such as {PAGE} and {PROGRAM}. The study’s header is written once, as default rows (a blank output_id), and each report adds its own lines:

spec$header[, c("line", "left", "center", "right")]
#>   line             left                                    center
#> 1    1   Example Pharma                                      <NA>
#> 2    2 Study XYZ-ONC-01                                      <NA>
#> 3    3             <NA>                                      <NA>
#> 4    4             <NA>                              Table 14.1.2
#> 5    5             <NA> Demographics and Baseline Characteristics
#> 6    6             <NA>                         Safety Population
#>                          right
#> 1        Clinical Study Report
#> 2 Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}
#> 3                         <NA>
#> 4                         <NA>
#> 5                         <NA>
#> 6                         <NA>

The report program 

cat(tfl_report_code(spec, content = "plan"), sep = "\n")
doc <- rtf_document(program = "C:\\study\\tfl\\DM", file = "output/DM.rtf") |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(
      list(
        c(l = "Example Pharma", r = "Clinical Study Report"),
        c(l = "Study XYZ-ONC-01", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
        c(c = ""),
        c(c = "Table 14.1.2"),
        c(c = "Demographics and Baseline Characteristics"),
        c(c = "Safety Population")
      )
    ),
    footer = rtf_footer(
      list(
        c(l = "SD: standard deviation; Min: minimum; Max: maximum; ECOG: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group."),
        c(l = "{PROGRAM}       Generated on: {DATETIME}")
      )
    )
  ) |>
  rtf_tables(plan)

The RTF 

doc <- tfl_report(spec, content = plan)
rtf <- file.path(study, tfl_report_path(spec))
dir.create(dirname(rtf), showWarnings = FALSE)
generate_rtfreport(doc, rtf, overwrite = TRUE)
file.exists(rtf)
#> [1] TRUE

The program a study keeps

Put together, the three pieces are one short program per output that a person can read top to bottom:

library(rtfreporter)
# 1 DATA    the ARD (programs/ard.R, written by tfl_ard_code())
ard <- readRDS("output/ard/ard.rds")
ard <- ard[ard$output_id == "DM", ]
# 2 TABLE   tfl_table_code(): the ARD normalized, then the plan
plan <- ard |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "TRT01A", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", ...) |>
  ...
# 3 REPORT  tfl_report_code()
doc <- rtf_document(program = "DM")
doc <- rtf_tables(doc, plan)
generate_rtfreport(doc, "output/DM.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)

When the spec cannot say it

A spec says the common things in columns. What it cannot express is written as R in the spec, in its code columns, so the program is still written from the spec and never edited by hand afterwards:

  • analysis_data$code: R that makes an analysis data;
  • analyses$code with method custom: R that makes an analysis’s ARD (tfl_ard_as_custom() writes an existing row as such code, to start from);
  • args, derive, where: R expressions where a value is code;
  • a figure design’s code steps and layer_code layers, and !r values.

And what is truly one report’s own – a cell style computed row by row, a step after the pages are made – is one more verb piped after the plan.

Where next

  • The ARD spec: datasets, populations, a report’s analysis data (subjects, keep, code), its code lists, the analyses.
  • The table spec: the table sheets, numbers or the ARD’s text, the decimals written once, a report’s code lists and the variables’ labels, and a plan written in code back to a workbook.
  • Reports: headers, footers, titles, footnotes and tokens written once for the study, each report’s own tokens, the company’s font and the setup code the report programs share.
  • Listings, Figures and CDISC ARS.
  • Working with an AI assistant? Attach tflspec_ai_manual(), the manual of the installed version.
